s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness during a long-haul flight with a background of autoimmune hemolytic anemia
key_facts: 58-year-old woman
Developed right arm weakness 8 hours into a long-haul flight
Medical history of Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Presented with dehydration
Blood film showed auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 119 mm/h
D-dimer was 24.7 nmol/L
Fibrinogen was 15.6 μmol/L
Renal function showed signs of dehydration
Elevated tumor markers
ECG and telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac chamber size and function
Brain MRI showed multiple small foci of restricted diffusion
Carotid ultrasound showed normal carotid and vertebral artery anatomy

shortlist.label: Embolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness and multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of autoimmune hemolytic anemia and elevated D-dimer

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated D-dimer, fibrinogen, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Cancer-associated thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated tumor markers and multiple echogenic targets in heart chambers

shortlist.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia suggested by auto-agglutination on blood film

raw.rationale: The patient has elevated tumor markers, which suggests an underlying malignancy. The presence of dehydration, auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells, elevated D-dimer, and fibrinogen levels, along with multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI, are consistent with a hypercoagulable state often seen in cancer-associated thrombosis.

rejected.label: Embolic stroke
rejected.why: While the patient has multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI, the presence of elevated tumor markers and a hypercoagulable state suggests a more complex underlying condition than a simple embolic stroke.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of autoimmune hemolytic anemia, there is no clear evidence of antiphospholipid antibodies, and the clinical presentation is more suggestive of a cancer-associated thrombosis.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen levels, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with a localized thrombotic event rather than a widespread disseminated intravascular coagulation.

rejected.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic pentad of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, including thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, renal failure, neurological symptoms, and fever.

gold: Cardioembolic stroke with underlying hypercoagulable state due to metastatic breast cancer and autoimmune hemolytic anemia
